INS-F01.name: Formal Rules & Authority Allocation
INS-F01.constructs: rules, rights, obligations, authority allocation and discretion
INS-F01.commonOperations: rule adoption, repeal and authority reallocation
INS-F01.majorOutcomes: implementation, review rights and constrained choice
INS-F01.identificationProblems: de jure text rarely identifies de facto operation
INS-F01.constructControversy: authority does not establish legitimacy or compliance
INS-F01.principalBoundary: formal obligation, restriction, authority, decision rights, realized enforcement, legitimacy and compliance remain distinct
INS-F01.acuteChronicOrPolicyTiming: Announcement, adoption, implementation, exposure, measurement, lag and persistence separated where relevant.

INS-F02.name: Incentives, Sanctions & Payoffs
INS-F02.constructs: rewards, fees, taxes, benefits, penalties, liability and contingencies
INS-F02.measurementConventions: statutory schedules, administrative receipt and perceived expectation
INS-F02.constructControversy: statutory magnitude is not received or expected magnitude
INS-F02.principalBoundary: formal incentives and sanctions differ from expected, received and perceived incentives, deterrence and behavior
INS-F02.acuteChronicOrPolicyTiming: Announcement, adoption, implementation, exposure, measurement, lag and persistence separated where relevant.

INS-F03.name: Administrative Burden & Procedural Friction
INS-F03.constructs: learning, documentation, procedural, time and channel burdens
INS-F03.measurementConventions: steps, time, documents, money and experience
INS-F03.commonOperations: simplification, assistance, recertification and channel changes
INS-F03.identificationProblems: outreach and simplification are often bundled
INS-F03.constructControversy: take-up is behavior and is not structural service coverage
INS-F03.principalBoundary: learning, documentation, compliance, time and psychological costs cannot be collapsed into one burden mechanism
INS-F03.acuteChronicOrPolicyTiming: Announcement, adoption, implementation, exposure, measurement, lag and persistence separated where relevant.

INS-F04.name: Organizational Structure & Work Design
INS-F04.constructs: centralization, hierarchy, specialization, span, workflow and caseload
INS-F04.measurementConventions: organization charts, workload ratios and process measures
INS-F04.commonOperations: organizational redesign, posting and discretion changes
INS-F04.majorOutcomes: expertise acquisition, effort, delay and service performance
INS-F04.constructControversy: formal structure does not prove realized workflow
INS-F04.principalBoundary: formal structure, work design, actual workflow, discretion, role clarity, caseload and performance are non-equivalent
INS-F04.acuteChronicOrPolicyTiming: Announcement, adoption, implementation, exposure, measurement, lag and persistence separated where relevant.

INS-F05.name: Monitoring, Enforcement & Accountability
INS-F05.constructs: monitoring, audit, disclosure, oversight, targets and accountability
INS-F05.measurementConventions: audit assignment, observed compliance and missing resources
INS-F05.commonOperations: audit probability, disclosure and oversight changes
INS-F05.moderators: elite capture, free riding and evaluator identity
INS-F05.identificationProblems: proxy outcomes and bundled accountability components
INS-F05.constructControversy: monitoring is not perceived monitoring or sanction certainty
INS-F05.principalBoundary: monitoring capacity, actual audit exposure, perceived monitoring, enforcement certainty and accountability consequences remain separate
INS-F05.acuteChronicOrPolicyTiming: Announcement, adoption, implementation, exposure, measurement, lag and persistence separated where relevant.

INS-F06.name: Participation, Procedural Governance & Redress
INS-F06.constructs: participation rights, representation, voice, reasons, impartiality and redress
INS-F06.measurementConventions: formal rights, observed procedure and recipient appraisal
INS-F06.majorOutcomes: fairness, legitimacy, cooperation and corrected decisions
INS-F06.identificationProblems: objective and perceived procedure commonly share method variance
INS-F06.constructControversy: voice alone cannot stand for a full procedural-justice package
INS-F06.principalBoundary: formal participation, actual voice, objective procedure, perceived fairness, redress use, legitimacy and compliance remain separate
INS-F06.acuteChronicOrPolicyTiming: Announcement, adoption, implementation, exposure, measurement, lag and persistence separated where relevant.

INS-F07.name: Resource Distribution, Eligibility & Service Access
INS-F07.constructs: budgets, coverage, rationing, priorities, access and gatekeeping
INS-F07.measurementConventions: budget records, eligible population, availability, receipt and use
INS-F07.majorOutcomes: coverage, uptake, receipt and service result
INS-F07.identificationProblems: policy assignment differs from realized exposure
INS-F07.constructControversy: availability, access, use and benefit cannot substitute
INS-F07.principalBoundary: allocation, eligibility, availability, accessibility, receipt, use and benefit are successive non-equivalent states
INS-F07.acuteChronicOrPolicyTiming: Announcement, adoption, implementation, exposure, measurement, lag and persistence separated where relevant.

INS-F08.name: Market, Labor & Transaction Structure
INS-F08.constructs: competition, concentration, barriers, transaction structure, ownership, employment protection and bargaining
INS-F08.mechanisms: entry, bargaining, matching and transaction costs
INS-F08.measurementConventions: market shares, rules, contracts and labor outcomes
INS-F08.identificationProblems: cross-market ecological comparisons and endogenous regulation
INS-F08.constructControversy: structure is not perceived security or individual outcome
INS-F08.principalBoundary: market concentration, competition, entry barriers, transaction costs, labor protection and individual economic experience require level alignment
INS-F08.acuteChronicOrPolicyTiming: Announcement, adoption, implementation, exposure, measurement, lag and persistence separated where relevant.

INS-F09.name: Political Power, Rights & Differential Treatment
INS-F09.constructs: formal and de facto power, rights, discrimination, segregation, vetoes, censorship and border rules
INS-F09.measurementConventions: legal coding, administrative disparities and experienced treatment
INS-F09.commonOperations: rights, electoral, censorship and enforcement reforms
INS-F09.majorOutcomes: representation, treatment, access and psychological appraisal
INS-F09.identificationProblems: de jure/de facto and institutional/person-level mismatch
INS-F09.constructControversy: formal rights do not establish realized protection
INS-F09.principalBoundary: de jure rights and power differ from de facto enforcement, differential treatment, lived experience and psychological efficacy
INS-F09.acuteChronicOrPolicyTiming: Announcement, adoption, implementation, exposure, measurement, lag and persistence separated where relevant.

INS-F10.name: Corruption, Patronage & Institutional Integrity
INS-F10.constructs: patronage, clientelism, corruption, bribery opportunity and integrity controls
INS-F10.measurementConventions: transactions, discrepancies, prosecutions and perception indices
INS-F10.majorOutcomes: missing resources, transactions, prevalence and trust
INS-F10.identificationProblems: perception measures and detected cases are endogenous proxies
INS-F10.constructControversy: one corruption proxy cannot establish broad prevalence
INS-F10.principalBoundary: corruption opportunity, transaction, prevalence, observation, experience, perception, integrity, trust and legitimacy are distinct
INS-F10.acuteChronicOrPolicyTiming: Announcement, adoption, implementation, exposure, measurement, lag and persistence separated where relevant.

INS-F11.name: Interorganizational & Multilevel Governance
INS-F11.constructs: resource dependence, interdependence, overlap, fragmentation and institutional pressures
INS-F11.measurementConventions: agreements, joint activity, dependencies and results
INS-F11.majorOutcomes: actual coordination, delay and joint performance
INS-F11.identificationProblems: formal partnership is not effective coordination
INS-F11.constructControversy: institutional pressure does not prove adoption or performance
INS-F11.principalBoundary: formal coordination arrangements, actual coordination, interdependence, joint capacity and collective performance remain distinct
INS-F11.acuteChronicOrPolicyTiming: Announcement, adoption, implementation, exposure, measurement, lag and persistence separated where relevant.

INS-F12.name: Policy Stability & Institutional Change
INS-F12.constructs: stability, switching costs, emergency authority, review, precedent and learning
INS-F12.measurementConventions: policy histories, implementation dates and organizational response
INS-F12.commonOperations: policy change, review and emergency powers
INS-F12.constructControversy: document change is not immediate system-state change
INS-F12.principalBoundary: announcement, adoption, implementation, enforcement, adaptation, stability and experienced uncertainty require explicit timing
INS-F12.acuteChronicOrPolicyTiming: Announcement, adoption, implementation, exposure, measurement, lag and persistence separated where relevant.

INS-F13.name: State Capacity & Legal-Institutional Quality
INS-F13.constructs: fiscal, staffing, administrative, legal, territorial, analytic and emergency capacity
INS-F13.measurementConventions: budgets, qualified staffing, reach, consistency and fidelity
INS-F13.majorOutcomes: implementation, reach, service and legal protection
INS-F13.moderators: task, jurisdiction, period and constituent overlap
INS-F13.identificationProblems: broad indices share indicators and outcomes may proxy latent capacity
INS-F13.constructControversy: capacity does not uniquely follow from performance
INS-F13.principalBoundary: capacity, staffing, reach, implementation fidelity, legal quality, service delivery, performance, trust and legitimacy are not interchangeable
INS-F13.acuteChronicOrPolicyTiming: Announcement, adoption, implementation, exposure, measurement, lag and persistence separated where relevant.
